data_points.source_name: Redseer (BPC in Quick Commerce article, Mar-2026)
data_points.notes: Channel: e-commerce (all online) — India online BPC GMV ~INR 52,000 cr CY25 (2.4x vs CY22). Cross-reference: Redseer separately reports INR 56,000 cr for FY26 (see FY26 claim) — CY vs FY basis differs.

Channel: e-commerce (all online) — India online BPC growth ~35% YoY FY26. Grooming +37% YoY; makeup & fragrance ~+30% YoY per same source.

data_points.notes: Channel: quick-commerce — ~2% share of India ONLINE BPC spending in CY22 (share of online BPC, NOT of total BPC retail).

data_points.notes: Channel: quick-commerce — ~16% share of India ONLINE BPC in CY25 (up from ~2% CY22; BPC GMV in q-commerce grew ~22.5x CY22-CY25). Share of online BPC, NOT total retail. Cross-reference: same firm reports 9% FY25 / ~18% FY26 on fiscal-year basis.

Channel: quick-commerce — 9% share of India ONLINE BPC in FY25 (share of online BPC, NOT total retail). Cross-reference: ~16% on CY25 basis per same firm's q-commerce article — period basis differs (FY vs CY).

data_points.methodology: Midpoint of Redseer's published 30-40% range; PROJECTION for 2030, not an actual.

data_points.source_name: Ladya (Blinkit commission and seller economics guide)
data_points.notes: Channel: q-commerce — Blinkit base commission, Beauty & Cosmetics category 18-22% of MRP (midpoint recorded; fragrances at top of range); Personal Care 16-20%. Commission charged on MRP, not discounted selling price.

data_points.source_name: Ladya (Blinkit commission and seller economics guide)
data_points.notes: Channel: q-commerce — Blinkit ALL-IN take for beauty category approx 38% (commission + fulfilment fees + payment gateway + platform fees + typical ad spend); personal care approx 32% all-in. Distinct from the 18-22% base commission.

Channel: q-commerce — Zepto overall take rate 22-23% (midpoint recorded), cited as part of pre-IPO profitability push. Same article: Blinkit moved to variable commission effective 13-Mar-2025 — 2% below INR 500, 6% for INR 500-700, 18% for INR 1,200+ (all categories, not BPC-specific).

data_points.source_name: Kirana Club (FMCG distribution in India guide 2026)
data_points.notes: Channel: general trade — kirana retailer margin on national brands with strong consumer pull: 5-10% (midpoint recorded); regional brands 10-18%. FMCG-wide guide, not BPC-specific; personal care noted as trust-driven but no separate % given.

data_points.source_name: Kirana Club (FMCG distribution in India guide 2026)
data_points.notes: Channel: general trade — kirana retailer margin demanded from NEW brands entering unfamiliar markets: 18-25%+ (midpoint of stated 18-25 recorded). Relevant benchmark for a K-beauty entrant in GT. FMCG-wide guide, not BPC-specific.

data_points.source_name: Kirana Club (FMCG distribution in India guide 2026)
data_points.notes: Channel: general trade — distributor ALL-IN cost for smaller brands: 20-30% of sale price (midpoint recorded), covering margin + credit losses + scheme funding + returns; higher than headline distributor margin alone. FMCG-wide, not BPC-specific.

data_points.source_name: Storewise (FMCG distribution margins and sales structure)
data_points.notes: Channel: general trade — distributor/substockist margin 12% in worked example (buys at INR 125, sells to retailer at INR 140 on INR 175 MRP product); superstockist 5-7%. Example is mid-size FMCG ready-to-eat segment; indicative of GT structure, not BPC-specific.

data_points.source_name: Storewise (FMCG distribution margins and sales structure)
data_points.notes: Channel: general trade — retailer margin 20% in same worked example (buys at INR 140, MRP INR 175). Example is mid-size FMCG ready-to-eat segment; indicative of GT structure, not BPC-specific. No modern-trade-specific margin found on any fetched page.

data_points.source_name: TheBK / Beauty Kyungjae (Korean beauty trade press)

data_points.source_name: TheBK / Beauty Kyungjae (Korean beauty trade press)
data_points.notes: Extracted from the same article as the per-capita-spend claims on file (not previously promoted to its own claim): total India BPC market USD 24bn in 2024. Value basis not stated by source; assumed consumer sell-through, consistent with the per-capita framing. cf Statista USD 28bn (2024, already on file) — ~14% lower, within normal aggregator variance (rule 7 threshold is 20%); cf Redseer USD 23bn FY25 and USD 27bn CY2025 (already on file) — same order of magnitude across sources. Organised/unorganised coverage not stated.

data_points.source_name: TheBK / Beauty Kyungjae (Korean beauty trade press)
data_points.notes: FORECAST VALUE from the same article as the per-capita-spend claims: total India BPC market projected at USD 45bn by 2030 (from USD 24bn 2024, implying ~11% CAGR). Value basis assumed consumer sell-through, not stated by source. cf Redseer USD 40bn by 2030 (from USD 23bn FY25) and USD 39bn by 2030 (from USD 27bn CY2025) already on file — all three 2030 forecasts cluster in the USD 39-45bn range despite different base years and sources.

data_points.source_name: TheBK / Beauty Kyungjae (Korean beauty trade press)
data_points.notes: [CORRIDOR] K-beauty products consumed in India, USD 400M in 2024, extracted from the same TheBK/Beauty Kyungjae article as the per-capita-spend claims already on file (not previously promoted to its own claim). This is India-side retail sizing of K-beauty demand, not Korea's export FOB flow (contrast with the UN Comtrade KR-to-IN export_value claims filed under KR segments). Value basis not stated by source; assumed consumer sell-through. Sits well below The Report Cubes' USD 0.335bn (2026) and Expert Market Research's INR 3139.31cr (2025, ~USD 0.335bn) K-beauty-in-India figures already on file — directionally consistent (same order of magnitude, later base year is higher), not a conflict. Organised/unorganised coverage not stated. Cross-segment corridor estimate (not attributable to a single taxonomy segment on this source), filed under total_bpc.

data_points.source_name: TheBK / Beauty Kyungjae (Korean beauty trade press)
data_points.notes: [CORRIDOR] FORECAST VALUE: K-beauty products consumed in India, projected USD 1.6bn by 2030 (from USD 400M 2024), per the same article as the paired 2024 market_size claim. cf Expert Market Research INR 32,424cr by 2035 (already on file, ~USD 3.37bn at the pinned rate) for a later, larger horizon on a similar growth trajectory. Value basis assumed consumer sell-through, not stated by source.

data_points.source_name: TheBK / Beauty Kyungjae (Korean beauty trade press)
data_points.methodology: Stated directly by the source ('growing 25.9%/yr'), not independently derived; internally consistent with its own paired endpoints (USD 400M 2024 to USD 1.6bn 2030: (1600/400)^(1/6)-1 = 25.99%, matching the stated rate).
data_points.notes: [CORRIDOR] K-beauty-in-India forecast growth rate 2024-2030. cf Expert Market Research 26.3% CAGR (2026-2035) and The Report Cubes 19.17% CAGR (to 2034) already on file — all cluster in the 19-26% range for K-beauty-in-India growth, a useful convergence despite different vendors and windows.
